title: Aegaeon: Effective GPU Pooling for Concurrent LLM Serving on the Market
technique: token-level auto-scaling and scheduling for multi-model GPU pooling: disaggregated prefill/decode instances, preemptive model switching, component reuse, explicit memory management, fine-grained KV synchronization

optimized_metrics.evidence: Aegaeon schedules both the request execution and the auto-scaling decisions in unison to maximize request SLO attainment.
Given a list of 𝑀 models to be served, our goal is to minimize the number of GPU instances 𝑁 required to meet the SLOs for all models through auto-scaling, thus maximizing resource usage.
quantifies SLOs as the ability to meet generation deadlines (i.e., the target TTFT and TBT metrics) on a per-token basis
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: setting TTFT to 10s and TBT to 100ms; SLO attainment is defined as the percentage of token generation times that meet their deadlines

optimized_metrics.evidence: setting TTFT to 10s and TBT to 100ms according to our internal criterion

headline_claim.text: Aegaeon sustains 2-2.5x higher request arrival rates or 1.5-9x more goodput compared to existing solutions ... reduces the number of GPUs required for serving these models from 1,192 to 213, highlighting an 82% GPU resource saving

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we define SLO attainment as the percentage of token generation times that meet their deadlines, which better reflects the end-user experience.
metric_definitions.locator: §2.1 (Fig 3 caption: 'the proportion of the green area')
metric_definitions.notes: per-token, not per-request: each token has a deadline (TTFT deadline for first, then TBT cadence with buffered output)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: (i) TTFT, which measures the latency to produce the initial output token
metric_definitions.notes: includes model auto-scaling and queueing delay across models (HOL blocking is the main motivation)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: (ii) TBT, which gauges the latency to generate each subsequent token
metric_definitions.notes: per-token deadline; single large TBT can be masked by buffering earlier tokens

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Vertical lines indicate the maximum goodput while meeting the 90% overall SLO requirement.
metric_definitions.notes: max per-model RPS at which overall SLO attainment >= 90%

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We report the SLO attainment as defined in §2.1, setting TTFT to 10s and TBT to 100ms according to our internal criterion for our online inference service, and also in alignment with industrial practices
metric_definitions.notes: stricter variants 0.5x/0.3x/0.2x (down to 2s TTFT / 20ms TBT); recommendation service uses 3s TTFT and 30ms TBT

slo_spec: TTFT 10 s and TBT 100 ms (internal criterion); stricter 0.5x/0.3x/0.2x down to 2 s / 20 ms; goodput at 90% overall attainment.
load_regime: request-rate sweep per model (RPS 0.1, 0.5, ...) with number of models varied (up to ~40+); production deployment
tradeoff_acknowledged: stricter SLOs reduce slack and GPU-pooling opportunity: under the strictest setup (0.2x SLO) Aegaeon no longer outperforms MuxServe; at 0.5x/0.3x it supports at least 50% / 12.5% more models; looser TBT allows more aggressive sharing
hardware: 2 nodes x 8 H800 80GB testbed (A10 4-GPU and 8xH800 sub-experiments); production H20 GPUs (1,192 -> 213)
models: 6B-14B Qwen/Llama/InternLM/Yi for main eval; 72B with TP in Fig 17; production 1.8B-72B
workloads: ShareGPT, ShareGPT-ix2, ShareGPT-ox2 (length-scaled); production traces on model marketplace
extractor_notes: Token-granularity SLO attainment (fraction of token deadlines met) differs from the common per-request attainment. Goodput = max RPS at 90% attainment (rate-based). Scheduler explicitly picks decode time quotas to minimize alpha = reciprocal of estimated SLO attainment. Full text from SOSP'25 PDF (ennanzhai.github.io), no arXiv version.
